title: Etale cohomology of the local scheme at a point as a colimit over Zariski neighbourhoods
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal F$ an abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], $x\in X$, $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ the local ring [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] and $g_x:\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}\to X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] the canonical morphism [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism]; for every open $U\ni x$ it factors uniquely as $g_x=j_U\circ g_{x,U}$ with $j_U:U\hookrightarrow X$ the open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. For an open $U\subseteq X$ write $H^q(U,\mathcal F)$ for the cohomology of $\mathcal F$ over the object $U\hookrightarrow X$ of $X_{\Et}$ (an open immersion is etale [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]; [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (2)), the restriction $H^q(U,\mathcal F)\to H^q(W,\mathcal F)$ for $W\subseteq U$ being induced by the restriction maps of an injective resolution of $\mathcal F$. Then $H^q(U,\mathcal F)=H^q(U_{\Et},j_U^{-1}\mathcal F)$ canonically, and the maps $H^q(U,\mathcal F)=H^q(U_{\Et},j_U^{-1}\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{g_{x,U}^*}H^q((\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x})_{\Et},g_{x,U}^{-1}j_U^{-1}\mathcal F)\cong H^q((\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x})_{\Et},g_x^{-1}\mathcal F)$ (pullback [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] followed by the canonical isomorphism $g_{x,U}^{-1}j_U^{-1}\cong g_x^{-1}$ of inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]; etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]) are compatible with the restrictions and induce, for every $q\ge0$, an isomorphism
$$\varinjlim_{U\ni x\ \text{open}}H^q(U,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^q((\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x})_{\Et},g_x^{-1}\mathcal F),$$
the colimit being over the open neighbourhoods of $x$ ordered by reverse inclusion (a directed set). In particular a class $\xi\in H^q(U,\mathcal F)$ whose image in $H^q((\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x})_{\Et},g_x^{-1}\mathcal F)$ is zero restricts to zero in $H^q(W,\mathcal F)$ for some open $x\in W\subseteq U$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09AX (lemma-local-rings-strictly-henselian), proof, line 14214-14218: 'the stalk at x is colim H^p_etale(U, F) = H^p_etale(Spec(O_{X,x}), G_x) ... see Lemma 03Q6' (lemma-directed-colimit-cohomology, line 7464, a special case of Theorem Tag 09YQ, theorem-colimit) applied to the affine open neighbourhoods U = Spec A of x, with O_{X,x} = colim A; the identification H^q(U, F) = H^q(U_etale, F|_U) is sites-cohomology.tex Lemma Tag 03F3 (lemma-cohomology-of-open)

proof.text: *The groups over open subsets and their identification with $H^q(U_{\Et},j_U^{-1}\mathcal F)$.* For an open $U\subseteq X$ the inclusion $j_U:U\hookrightarrow X$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], so it is an object of $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and for opens $W\subseteq U$ the inclusion is a morphism of $X_{\Et}$. $\textit{Ab}(X_{\Et})$ has enough injectives ([def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (1)); fix once and for all an injective resolution $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ in $\textit{Ab}(X_{\Et})$, so that $H^q(U,\mathcal F)=H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(U))$ and the restriction $r_{UW}:H^q(U,\mathcal F)\to H^q(W,\mathcal F)$ is $H^q$ of the restriction maps $\mathcal I^\bullet(U)\to\mathcal I^\bullet(W)$ ([def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (2)). By [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] (5) applied to the etale $u=j_U$, $j_U^{-1}\mathcal F\to j_U^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet$ is a resolution of $j_U^{-1}\mathcal F$ by a bounded below complex of injective abelian sheaves on $U_{\Et}$, hence a K-injective resolution [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and $H^q(U_{\Et},j_U^{-1}\mathcal F)=\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(U,j_U^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet))$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Let $\rho^U_{\mathcal G}:j_U^{-1}\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal G|_U$ be the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (1), natural in $\mathcal G\in\textit{Ab}(X_{\Et})$; its sections over $U$ are isomorphisms $\rho^U_{\mathcal I^p}(U):\Gamma(U,j_U^{-1}\mathcal I^p)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal I^p|_U(U)=\mathcal I^p(U)$ which, by naturality in $\mathcal G$ applied to the differentials $\mathcal I^p\to\mathcal I^{p+1}$, form an isomorphism of complexes $\Gamma(U,j_U^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal I^\bullet(U)$. Define $\iota_U:H^q(U,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(U_{\Et},j_U^{-1}\mathcal F)$ as $\mathcal H^q$ of its inverse. This is the canonical identification of the statement: for a second injective resolution $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I'^\bullet$ and a morphism of complexes $\alpha:\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal I'^\bullet$ over $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F}$, $j_U^{-1}\alpha$ is a morphism of resolutions of $j_U^{-1}\mathcal F$ over the identity, and naturality of $\rho^U$ gives $\rho^U_{\mathcal I'}(U)\circ\Gamma(U,j_U^{-1}\alpha)=\alpha(U)\circ\rho^U_{\mathcal I}(U)$; so the two $\iota_U$ correspond under the identifications $\mathcal H^q(\alpha(U))$ and $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(U,j_U^{-1}\alpha))$ of the groups computed from different resolutions ([def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (2), [prop-weil-pbc-cohomology-resolution-independent], and the description of $H^q(\varphi)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]).

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F3 (lemma-cohomology-of-open, line 608), part (2) and its proof (restriction of an injective resolution to U is an injective resolution), for the etale site with $X_{\etale}/U=U_{\etale}$ (etale-cohomology.tex Section Tag 03S2, j^{-1} is restriction)

proof.text: *Restrictions are pullbacks along the inclusions.* Let $W\subseteq U\subseteq X$ be opens, $j_{WU}:W\hookrightarrow U$ the inclusion, so $j_W=j_U\circ j_{WU}$, and let $c$ be the composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]. Claim: $\iota_W\circ r_{UW}=H^q(c_{j_U,j_{WU},\mathcal F})\circ j_{WU}^*\circ\iota_U$, with $j_{WU}^*$ the pullback [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. (a) *A section identity.* For $\mathcal G\in\textit{Ab}(X_{\Et})$ we show $\rho^W_{\mathcal G}(W)=\rho^U_{\mathcal G}(W)\circ\rho^{WU}_{j_U^{-1}\mathcal G}(W)\circ c_{j_U,j_{WU},\mathcal G}(W)^{-1}$ as maps $\Gamma(W,j_W^{-1}\mathcal G)\to\mathcal G(W)$, where $\rho^{WU}$ is the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (1) for $j_{WU}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-restriction-pullback-unit] to $g=j_U:U\to X$ and the open $W\subseteq X$: then $W'=j_U^{-1}(W)=W$, $j_{W'}=j_{WU}$, $g_W=\mathrm{id}_W$, $h=j_W$, and for $a\in\Gamma(W,j_W^{-1}\mathcal G)$ it gives $\rho^{WU}_{j_U^{-1}\mathcal G}(W)\bigl(c_{j_U,j_{WU}}(W)^{-1}c_{j_W,\mathrm{id}_W}(W)\,\eta_{\mathrm{id}_W}(W)(a)\bigr)=\eta_{j_U,\mathcal G}(W)\bigl(\rho^W_{\mathcal G}(W)(a)\bigr)$. Here $c_{j_W,\mathrm{id}_W}=e_Wj_W^{-1}$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition] (1) and $e_{W,\mathcal H}\circ d_{W,\mathrm{id}^{-1}\mathcal H}\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id}_W,\mathcal H}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal H}$ [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (3), $d_W(W)$ being the identification $W\times_WW=W$; so $c_{j_W,\mathrm{id}_W}(W)\eta_{\mathrm{id}_W}(W)(a)=a$. On the right, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (2) for $j_U$ and the object $W$ of $X_{\Et}$ says $\rho^U_{\mathcal G}(W\times_XU)\circ\eta_{j_U,\mathcal G}(W)$ is the restriction of $\mathcal G$ along $W\times_XU\to W$, which is the identity of $\mathcal G(W)$ under $W\times_XU=W$ ($W\subseteq U$, [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product]); so $\eta_{j_U,\mathcal G}(W)=\rho^U_{\mathcal G}(W)^{-1}$. Substituting gives (a). (b) *The claim.* By step 1, $j_U^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet$ is an injective resolution of $j_U^{-1}\mathcal F$, so [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] (5) for the etale $u=j_{WU}$ computes $j_{WU}^*$ as $\mathcal H^q$ of the restriction $\Gamma(U,j_U^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet)\to(j_U^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet)(W)$ followed by $\rho^{WU}_{j_U^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet}(W)^{-1}$ into $\Gamma(W,j_{WU}^{-1}j_U^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet)$; and $H^q(c_{j_U,j_{WU},\mathcal F})$ is $\mathcal H^q$ of $\Gamma(W,c_{j_U,j_{WU},\mathcal I^\bullet})$, since $c_{\mathcal I^\bullet}$ is a morphism between the injective resolutions $j_{WU}^{-1}j_U^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet$ and $j_W^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet$ (step 1) lying over $c_{\mathcal F}$ by naturality of $c$ (description of $H^q(\varphi)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]). For a cocycle $s\in\mathcal I^p(U)$, $\rho^U_{\mathcal I^p}$ being a morphism of sheaves on $U_{\Et}$ commutes with restriction along $W\to U$, so the right-hand side of the claim sends the class of $s$ to the class of $c(W)\rho^{WU}(W)^{-1}\rho^U_{\mathcal I^p}(W)^{-1}(s|_W)$, which is $\rho^W_{\mathcal I^p}(W)^{-1}(s|_W)$ by (a); this is $\iota_W(r_{UW}[s])$.

proof.text: *The limit theorem on the affine neighbourhoods.* Let $N_x$ be the directed set of affine open neighbourhoods of $x$ of [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-spec-limit-affine-neighbourhoods]: by its clauses (1)-(3), $(W,j_{W'W})_{W\in N_x}$ is a directed inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, whose limit is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with projections $g_{x,W}$. Put $\mathcal F_W=j_W^{-1}\mathcal F$ on $W_{\Et}$ and $\varphi_{W'W}=c_{j_W,j_{W'W},\mathcal F}:j_{W'W}^{-1}j_W^{-1}\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{W'}^{-1}\mathcal F$ [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]. The cocycle condition $\varphi_{W''W}=\varphi_{W''W'}\circ j_{W''W'}^{-1}\varphi_{W'W}$ for $W''\subseteq W'\subseteq W$ (with $j_{W''W}^{-1}$ identified with $j_{W''W'}^{-1}j_{W'W}^{-1}$ through $c_{j_{W'W},j_{W''W'}}$) is the associativity of $c$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition] (1) for $u=j_W$, $v=j_{W'W}$, $w=j_{W''W'}$. So [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-limit-of-schemes] applies: with $\mathcal F_\infty=\varinjlim_Wg_{x,W}^{-1}\mathcal F_W$ (transition maps $\psi_{W'W}=g_{x,W'}^{-1}\varphi_{W'W}\circ c_{j_{W'W},g_{x,W'}}^{-1}$, coprojections $\kappa_W$), the maps $H^q(\kappa_W)\circ g_{x,W}^*:H^q(W_{\Et},j_W^{-1}\mathcal F)\to H^q((\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x})_{\Et},\mathcal F_\infty)$ induce an isomorphism from the colimit over $N_x$ of the groups $H^q(W_{\Et},j_W^{-1}\mathcal F)$, with transition maps $H^q(\varphi_{W'W})\circ j_{W'W}^*$, for every $q\ge0$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03Q6 (lemma-directed-colimit-cohomology, line 7464), 'a special case of Theorem Tag 09YQ' (theorem-colimit, line 7400), as cited in the proof of 09AX (line 14214-14218); applied to the affine open neighbourhoods of $x$ as in literature/stacks-project/limits.tex, proof of Lemma Tag 0GWT, line 1561-1564

proof.text: *The colimit sheaf is $g_x^{-1}\mathcal F$.* Put $\alpha_W=c_{j_W,g_{x,W},\mathcal F}:g_{x,W}^{-1}j_W^{-1}\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}g_x^{-1}\mathcal F$ [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]. For $W'\subseteq W$, the associativity of $c$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition] (1) for $u=j_W$, $v=j_{W'W}$, $w=g_{x,W'}$ (so $u\circ v=j_{W'}$, $v\circ w=g_{x,W}$) gives $c_{j_{W'},g_{x,W'}}\circ g_{x,W'}^{-1}(c_{j_W,j_{W'W}})=c_{j_W,g_{x,W}}\circ c_{j_{W'W},g_{x,W'}}$, i.e. $\alpha_{W'}\circ\psi_{W'W}=\alpha_W$. Hence the isomorphisms $\alpha_W$ carry the system $(g_{x,W}^{-1}\mathcal F_W,\psi)$ to the constant system with value $g_x^{-1}\mathcal F$ and identity transition maps, whose colimit is $g_x^{-1}\mathcal F$ with identity coprojections ($N_x$ is nonempty and directed, hence connected) [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-constant-connected-diagram]. So the $\alpha_W$ form a colimit cocone of $(g_{x,W}^{-1}\mathcal F_W,\psi)$, and by uniqueness of colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] there is an isomorphism $\beta:\mathcal F_\infty\xrightarrow{\sim}g_x^{-1}\mathcal F$ with $\beta\circ\kappa_W=\alpha_W$ for all $W$. Composing the isomorphism of step 4 with $H^q(\beta)$: the maps $H^q(\alpha_W)\circ g_{x,W}^*=H^q(c_{j_W,g_{x,W},\mathcal F})\circ g_{x,W}^*$ induce an isomorphism $\varinjlim_{W\in N_x}H^q(W_{\Et},j_W^{-1}\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q((\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x})_{\Et},g_x^{-1}\mathcal F)$.

proof.text: *Back to $H^q(W,\mathcal F)$, and cofinality.* By step 2 (for $W'\subseteq W$ in $N_x$), $\iota_{W'}\circ r_{WW'}=H^q(\varphi_{W'W})\circ j_{W'W}^*\circ\iota_W$, so the isomorphisms $\iota_W$ of step 1 form an isomorphism of directed systems over $N_x$ from $(H^q(W,\mathcal F),r)$ to the system of step 4, and $H^q(c_{j_W,g_{x,W}})\circ g_{x,W}^*\circ\iota_W=\theta_W$ by definition (step 3). Hence, by step 5, the $\theta_W$ ($W\in N_x$) induce an isomorphism $\varinjlim_{W\in N_x}H^q(W,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q((\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x})_{\Et},g_x^{-1}\mathcal F)$. Regard the open neighbourhoods of $x$ with the inclusions as morphisms as a cofiltered category $\mathcal I$ and $N_x$ as a full subcategory; every open $U\ni x$ contains some $W\in N_x$ [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-spec-limit-affine-neighbourhoods] (1). By [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory] (1), applied to the functor $U\mapsto H^q(U,\mathcal F)$ on $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}$, the canonical map $\varinjlim_{W\in N_x}H^q(W,\mathcal F)\to\varinjlim_{U\ni x}H^q(U,\mathcal F)$ induced by the coprojections is an isomorphism. Its composite with $\bar\theta$ of step 3 is the map induced by the $\theta_W$, $W\in N_x$ (both agree on each coprojection, [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]), which is an isomorphism; hence $\bar\theta$ is an isomorphism for every $q\ge0$.

proof.text: *The last assertion.* Let $\xi\in H^q(U,\mathcal F)$ with $\theta_U(\xi)=0$ and let $\lambda_U$ be the coprojection into $\varinjlim_{U'\ni x}H^q(U',\mathcal F)$. Then $\bar\theta(\lambda_U(\xi))=\theta_U(\xi)=0$, and $\bar\theta$ is injective (step 6), so $\lambda_U(\xi)=0$. The colimit is a filtered colimit of abelian groups ($\mathbb Z$-modules) over a directed set, so by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] (2) there is an open $W$ with $x\in W\subseteq U$ and $r_{UW}(\xi)=0$ in $H^q(W,\mathcal F)$.

split_report.summary: Split along the proof of Stacks 09AX ('the stalk at x is colim H^p(U,F) = H^p(Spec O_{X,x}, G_x), see 03Q6'), with 03Q6 taken as the special case of 09YQ (existing reviewed node lem-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-limit-of-schemes) applied to the directed system of affine open neighbourhoods of x, whose limit is Spec O_{X,x} (Limits, proof of 0GWT; new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-spec-limit-affine-neighbourhoods, which also carries the cofinality of the affine neighbourhoods and the unique factorization g_x = j_U o g_{x,U}). Seven steps: (1) H^q(U,F) = H^q(U_et, j_U^{-1}F) through the restricted injective resolution (03F3 (2); existing nodes cohomology-pullback-functorial (5) and etale-inverse-image-restriction (1)); (2) under it, restrictions are pullbacks along the inclusions composed with c (agent-written; from open-restriction-pullback-unit, inverse-image-composition (3) and the unit law of derived-inverse-image-composition (1)); (3) the maps theta_U of the statement are compatible with restrictions (functoriality (3),(4) of the pullback and associativity of c); (4) the limit theorem on the affine neighbourhoods; (5) the colimit sheaf is g_x^{-1}F (constant connected diagram); (6) identification of the systems and cofinality (colimit-initial-full-subcategory (1)); (7) the last assertion (filtered colimits elementwise). New Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale (Etale.instOfIsOpenImmersion, Etale.lean:78) for the objects U -> X of X_et used by the statement. Statement unchanged in content; citations added for the stalk, the canonical morphism, open immersions being etale and the composition isomorphisms of inverse images, and the four ids added to stmt_deps. The citer lem-weil-pbc-gabber-strict-henselian-zariski-comparison (step 3) uses exactly the colimit isomorphism over all opens and the last assertion, both proved here.
